theme: Length-of-stay, party-size and trip-purpose survey microdata (NTTO SIAT, UK IPS, Eurostat tour_dem, Japan travel survey, national travel surveys)
queries_run: gh search repos "international passenger survey" --sort stars
gh search repos "tour_dem eurostat OR eurostat tourism demand" --sort stars
gh search repos "length of stay tourism survey" --sort stars
gh search repos "NTTO SIAT OR survey international air travelers" --sort stars
gh search repos "japan travel survey OR JNTO OR trip purpose survey" --sort stars
gh search repos "national travel survey trip purpose party size" --sort stars
gh search repos "IPS ONS travel survey" --sort stars

candidates.name: DSDP_Project1 (ONS/LIDA International Passenger Survey replacement)
candidates.what_it_holds: Leeds Institute for Data Analytics (LIDA) x ONS Data Scientist Development Programme project to replace the UK International Passenger Survey (IPS) with non-survey sources (Mastercard transaction data, mobile/accommodation data mentioned) using ML. process.ipynb documents methodology exploring IPS microdata (trip purpose, expenditure, nationality) and candidate replacement signals. MIT license. No confirmed committed IPS microdata in-repo (references UK Data Service study 9279 as source).
candidates.why_useful: IPS covers exactly the trip-purpose/party-composition/length-of-stay microdata this theme targets, and this repo documents both the IPS variable structure and non-survey proxies (card spend) that could stand in for a discontinued/lagged survey -- relevant to gap on inbound trip-purpose mix and nowcasting substitutes.
candidates.size_hint: small (notebook + docs, no bulk data confirmed)

candidates.name: IPS-mlops
candidates.what_it_holds: MLOps pipeline (data cleaning, feature engineering, model training/eval) built on the UK International Passenger Survey 2023 dataset (252,260 individual passenger records, Jan-Dec 2023). Source data lives at UK Data Service study 9279 (https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/9279), not committed to the repo itself.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms IPS 2023 microdata exists at UK Data Service with row-level trip records (trip purpose, party info typically included in IPS schema); repo's pipeline code shows which fields matter and gives a working ETL to adapt if UKDS access is obtained.

candidates.name: ONS-LTIM-Passenger-Survey-4.01
candidates.what_it_holds: ONS Long-Term International Migration (LTIM) estimates derived from the International Passenger Survey: table 4.01, citizenship group by sex by age by country of last/next residence. Part of the GSS (Government Statistical Service) Cogs data-pipeline conversion of ONS reference tables to tidy CSV/CSVW.
candidates.why_useful: Same underlying IPS instrument as the trip-purpose tables, but this specific table is migration-flow demographics, not tourism trip-purpose/length-of-stay -- limited direct use, mainly confirms IPS-derived data is published in machine-readable form by GSS-Cogs (worth checking sibling repos for a trip-purpose/duration table).
candidates.size_hint: single reference table, historical ONS release

candidates.name: ONS-LTIM-Passenger-Survey-4.02
candidates.what_it_holds: Companion GSS-Cogs table: IPS-derived migration to/from the UK by main reason for migration, by citizenship groups.
candidates.why_useful: Same caveat as 4.01 -- IPS-sourced but migration-reason, not trip-purpose/party-size/length-of-stay for tourism. Low direct relevance; flags that the GSS-Cogs org (github.com/GSS-Cogs) is a broader source of ONS/IPS-derived tidy-data repos worth a follow-up scout with topic search.

candidates.name: Eurostat-Tourism-Data-Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed analysis project pulling and analyzing Eurostat tourism statistics (domain likely includes tour_occ / tour_dem series covering nights spent, trip purpose, duration bands by country). No confirmed row counts; a code-based acquisition/analysis pipeline against the Eurostat API rather than a static committed dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Eurostat's tour_dem dataset (EU demand-side tourism trips survey: purpose, duration, party/travel-group where available) is exactly the target series for this theme; this repo is a working example of pulling it programmatically, saving a fresh Eurostat API integration.
candidates.time_coverage: current Eurostat tour_dem vintages (survey runs ~2012-present, annual)

candidates.name: Eurostat-Tourism-Data-Analysis-in-Python
candidates.what_it_holds: Python script to download Eurostat tourism data via API for European tourism analysis. Similar scope to the kontogiannisg repo; a second independent implementation of a Eurostat tourism-data pull.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative/backup Eurostat API client if the other repo's approach is stale or uses a deprecated endpoint; same tour_dem/tour_occ relevance as above.
candidates.size_hint: small script repo, no bulk data

candidates.name: eurostat-tourism
candidates.what_it_holds: Eurostat data processing and visualization project, general tourism focus; details of exact dataset codes (tour_dem vs tour_occ vs tour_cap) not confirmed without deeper inspection.
candidates.why_useful: Another candidate Eurostat tourism-data pipeline; lower confidence than the two above on whether it touches the demand-side (trip purpose/duration) tables specifically versus capacity/occupancy tables.

notes: Coverage for this theme on GitHub is thin: the sanctioned instruments (NTTO SIAT, UK IPS, Eurostat tour_dem, Japan travel survey) are all restricted/licensed microdata sources (UK Data Service, Eurostat bulk-download portal, Japan Tourism Agency), so what GitHub actually holds is (a) ETL/analysis scripts that pull the public aggregate tables via API, not row-level survey microdata, and (b) one real find -- the LIDA/ONS DSDP_Project1 repo -- documenting the IPS variable schema and a live effort to replace it with non-survey proxies (Mastercard transactions), which is conceptually close to what this project would want if it ever tried to nowcast trip-purpose mix. No repos surfaced for NTTO SIAT (US survey of international air travelers) or a Japan national travel survey at all across 3 targeted queries -- likely because these are published only as PDF/Excel tables by the sponsoring agencies (US ITA/NTTO, Japan Tourism Agency) with no GitHub mirror activity. GSS-Cogs (github.com/GSS-Cogs) looks like a broader ONS-data-pipeline org worth a dedicated follow-up scout (topic or org search) since it may have additional IPS-derived tourism tables (trip purpose, average stay) beyond the two migration tables found here. Rate limiting was not encountered across the 6 gh search calls made.
